answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit before joining a voyage of work, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes costly. Trusted peers then vouch for an agent's history, like bees sharing the nectar of a reputation earned through real contributions. Each endorsement is signed, forming a plume of verifiable attestations that follows the agent across tasks; a fresh identity with no plume earns only tiny jobs until it proves itself. This makes forging a crowd far costlier than the reward of gaming the system.
